budget_interpretation.guide_clearance_budget: Independent +/- radial guide-radius budget, not diameter budget and not a measured printer tolerance.
budget_interpretation.gate_position_budget: Each finger has independent +/- radial center error; each gate plane has independent +/- axial error, giving twice this budget in relative gate spacing.
budget_interpretation.other_print_clearances: radial_print_clearance enlarges the nominal radial-hole radius according to its CAD expression; it is not additionally counted as a hole-size manufacturing tolerance. axial_print_clearance is an assembly design gap, not automatically a manufacturing error.
budget_interpretation.tip_radius: Exact spherical cap radius from SCAD; no separate tip-size, wear, seam, ovality or angular-misalignment tolerance has been supplied.
budget_interpretation.guide_axial_endpoints: Nominal start and length from SCAD; the gate axial-position budget is included in the ball envelope, but no additional measured guide-length/placement tolerance has been supplied.
budget_interpretation.ball_envelope: 40-41 mm is a selected analysis envelope read from parameters; not a statement of the user's measured balls or a sport standard.

model_assumptions: Rigid perfect spheres; the recognized cylindrical guide with aligned round side holes constrains centers to the enclosing disk e=sqrt(A^2-hole_radius^2)-sqrt(R^2-hole_radius^2). This holds for all lateral directions in the interior connected component, not just centers aligned with a hole.
Opposed spherical caps of equal radius have centers in one gate plane; radial cylindrical shanks extend outward and do not protrude farther into the ball-center disk.

The two X-directed through-holes (four wall openings) are included by a recognized CSG source contract and a continuous enclosing bound. Additional bypass ports, seams, joints, slots or guide-end escape paths are not inherited. Outward cylindrical rods are covered only by the ideal radial capsule condition, not by a parsed assembled solid model.
Insertion proof starts with the first ball parked against the closed front gate and a second ball touching it, with no shell deformation.

Every lateral ball center is allowed anywhere in its side-hole-expanded enclosing disk, a deliberately larger domain than the true anisotropic feasible set. This includes unequal mixed-diameter balls and opposite-wall offsets.
The candidate cam law is explicitly defined in this report; parameters alone do not specify or prove manufactured cam tracks.

guide_fit.cad_axis_convention: CAD z is the feed axis; front gate nominal z=0 and rear gate nominal z=-gate_spacing. The pair derivation uses x for the same axis.
guide_fit.axial_envelope_formula: upstream=-gate_budget-h_max-2*R_max-R_max; downstream=+gate_budget-h_min+R_max. Full sphere extents, all diameter mixtures and bounded lateral offsets are included conservatively.
guide_fit.axial_placement_caveat: Full stationary parked-pair extents fit only if both reported margins are positive. Nominal round-hole eccentricity is included; moving arrival/departure through ends, entrance transitions, hole manufacturing error and additional bypass/slot cuts remain unverified.

source_contract.scope: The unsectioned guide() CSG dimensions/topology only. section_view=true deliberately removes material and is excluded. This is not an evaluated mesh or manufacturing inspection.

continuous_proof.domain: Rigid perfect sphere center in the guide's interior connected component, with its equatorial plane inside the unsectioned cylindrical guide.
continuous_proof.parameter_envelope: The bound increases with guide radius A and hole radius h, and decreases with sphere radius R. Thus A_max and R_min bound the whole declared continuous parameter envelope; h is nominal because no manufacturing allowance for hole radius was supplied.
continuous_proof.equatorial_slice: At axial center z, a round X-directed hole removes only arcs with |Y|<k, where k=sqrt(max(0,h^2-(z-z_hole)^2))<=h. With two aligned holes, use the largest k at that slice; their union does not widen this Y band.
continuous_proof.directional_bound: Let alpha=asin(k/A), and theta be the direction from the nearer +/-X axis. If |theta|>=alpha, e<=A-R. Otherwise delta=alpha-|theta| and e<=A*cos(delta)-sqrt(R^2-A^2*sin(delta)^2).
continuous_proof.all_direction_argument: The directional limit increases with delta when A>R and k<R. Thus its maximum is on the hole axis (theta=0), and then increases with k up to h. This establishes the bound for all lateral directions and all interior axial positions.
continuous_proof.three_dimensional_attainment: For center (e,0,0) on one hole axis, the closest surviving wall has X=sqrt(A^2-Y^2), Z^2=max(0,h^2-Y^2). Squared distance decreases with Y^2 up to h^2 and increases thereafter; its minimum is at Y=+/-h,Z=0. The global bound is attained there for a single round hole. Additional aligned holes only remove material; the equatorial necessary bound still applies.
continuous_proof.disconnected_exterior: Ball centers already outside the tube are a different feasible component. This theorem does not assert a bound on arbitrary points in exterior space or prevent entering around an open tube end.

gate_blocking.formula: max_(y^2+z^2<=e^2) min(|(y,z)-(c_plus,0)|, |(y,z)-(-c_minus,0)|) < R+r; for symmetric tips this is sqrt(c^2+e^2)<R+r.
gate_blocking.closed_witness_scope: Worst point of the expanded enclosing disk; this particular off-axis point need not be physically reachable in the perforated guide. Its positive margin is a sufficient all-position bound.
gate_blocking.open_formula: c_open_min-R_min-e(A_max,R_min,hole_radius)-tip_radius>0. R+e(A,R,h) decreases with R, so the smallest sphere supplies the largest radial reach.

coaxial_touching_ball_window.formula_equal_balls: h=sqrt((R+r)^2-c^2); 2*h <= L <= 2*R. Equality is contact, not design margin.
coaxial_touching_ball_window.formula_mixed_balls: h1+h_rear1 <= L <= h1+(R1+R2)-h_rear2; equal front/rear geometries give 2*h1 <= L <= h1+R1+R2-h2.

eccentric_touching_ball_window.continuous_bound: h_min <= each front stop depth <= h_max; axial touching pitch >= p_min. Sufficient interval: 2*h_max <= L <= h_min+p_min-h_max. Independent worst cases make this conservative, not a necessary condition.
eccentric_touching_ball_window.extrema_basis: Use E(R)=sqrt(A_max^2-hole_radius^2)-sqrt(R^2-hole_radius^2). h_min^2=(R+tip)^2-c_max^2-E(R)^2 increases with R. For h_max^2, put C=sqrt(A_max^2-hole_radius^2), q=c_min-C: h_max^2=hole_radius^2+2*R*tip+tip^2-q^2-2*q*sqrt(R^2-hole_radius^2). If q<=0 this increases; if q>0 it is convex, so a maximum is always at a radius endpoint. Mixed-pair pitch is bounded by sqrt((2*R_min)^2-(2*E(R_min))^2). These arguments cover continuous mixtures, not just sampled diameters.
eccentric_touching_ball_window.full_sweep_condition: Radial closure is monotone and both tip centers remain radially outside the allowed ball-center disk. Under that condition the final tip positions are closest to each stationary ball.

sampled_cross_check.method: Direct sphere versus both spherical tips, including unequal left/right tip offsets, touching mixed-size balls, and boundary/interior centers of the side-hole-expanded enclosing disks.
sampled_cross_check.scope: Sampled cross-check only; continuous coverage is provided by the separate conservative interval bound. Requires the first ball to be seated at the front gate. The expanded disks are a superset of physical center positions; any intersection reported in them alone is a conservative-screen failure, not a proven physically reachable collision.

static_closed_pocket_capacity.formula: Any ball center between both closed gate planes must lie at least h_min from each. Its axial interval has length <= L_max-2*h_min. Two nonintersecting spheres need axial center spacing >= p_min.
static_closed_pocket_capacity.scope: This excludes two rigid balls wholly between two closed blocking gates. It does not prove successful loading, departing-ball clearance, or a full dynamic cycle.

profile.return: Traverse exactly the same position curve in reverse; partial reversal remains on that curve only with positive captive linkage.

cam_and_actual_position_interlock.geometric_invariant: For every trigger position, at least one actual gate center radius is below the worst-case blocking threshold; this is about actual positions, not commanded timing.
cam_and_actual_position_interlock.continuous_argument: With nonnegative overlap, at least one commanded gate remains fully closed throughout each linear segment and the central dwell; include the stated outward center-position budget in its blocking test.
required_physical_constraints: Each of four sliders must follow its actual closed-track cam; obstruction of either slider must prevent further common trigger travel before the other gate opens.
No follower escape, spring override, unbudgeted groove clearance, sliding pin, linkage buckling or housing deflection may let the trigger bypass a stalled gate.
A gate means both opposed fingers and their guide restrictions, not the average position of two independent fingers.
One-ball pocket capacity and departure/arrival state must be separately demonstrated; this invariant alone is not an exactly-one release proof.

asynchronous_counterexamples.case: Late ball centered on the rear gate plane during closure
asynchronous_counterexamples.outcome_with_positive_rigid_cam: The trigger stalls with the front gate still closed; no claim of smooth cycling or absence of ball damage.

outcome_if_linkage_can_override.meaning: A geometrically open path exists if both rear fingers remain retracted here while the front opens. This is a counterexample to timing-only assurance, not a simulated double shot.

asynchronous_counterexamples.case: Trigger pressed before any ball is seated
asynchronous_counterexamples.outcome: Rear can close and front open around an empty pocket; an arriving ball remains upstream. Exactly one shot per press is impossible without a ready condition or a wait/arming mechanism.

asynchronous_counterexamples.case: Return starts while released ball still intersects the front gate closing sweep
asynchronous_counterexamples.outcome: A rigid cam can stall or load the ball shell. Feed speed, trigger reversal and spin-pad drag are absent from this static calculation.

not_covered: Dynamic arrival, feed pauses, rebounding, changing lateral positions while inserting a finger, trigger velocity and arbitrary partial-cycle timing.
Exactly-one output, pocket occupancy through the moving portions of the cycle, and exit clearance before gate return.
Ball shell stiffness, denting, buckling, seams, real ovality, wear, dirt or sphere-size distribution outside the candidate envelope.
Finger/cam/follower/housing stiffness, finite follower size, groove undercut, contact stress, friction, spring force and mechanical return reliability.
Complete assembled shanks/slots/fasteners, guide-end transition motion, unrecognized extra openings, actual hole-size/shape tolerance, assembly access and printability.
Air bypass pressure loss, pneumatic force, feeder hose bends, guide transitions and adjustable spin-pad drag.
Printer calibration, measured dimensions, physical assembly, damage inspection and repeated end-to-end firing.
interpretation: A useful static candidate screen only. No CAD mechanism completion, simulation of motion/contact/airflow, physical reliability or first-print guarantee is claimed.
